name: NY-08
label: Safe D

model.rationale: Jeffries, the House Democratic leader, holds a D+24 seat with massive fundraising and no serious opposition spending against him; the Republican has raised essentially nothing. Fundamentals and markets both point to an overwhelming Democratic margin.
model.watch: A surprise independent or third-party surge, or Jeffries being diverted by national leadership duties, is the only realistic source of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Hakeem Jeffries, the House Democratic leader, seeks another term in a Brooklyn-based district that leans Democratic by about 24 points. He has raised nearly $15 million and holds $5 million on hand, while Republican challenger Lewis Mizrahi reports no meaningful fundraising and draws no outside support. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Jeffries' win probability around 96 percent.

The fundamentals point to a lopsided Democratic margin, with incumbency and money adding to the district's inherent lean. The main uncertainty is simply how many voters turn out for a race with little competition, which affects the size of the margin more than the outcome.
